content.content:
1	Temperature-sensitive goods such as vaccines, biological samples, prepared meals and laboratory reagents are frequently shipped in insulated carriers that hold a payload within a target temperature band for a period of hours or days. Carriers of this general kind fall into two broad families. Powered carriers use a fan, a pump or another driven air mover, together with a power source, to force air over a cold source and through the payload space. Passive carriers omit the power source and rely on conduction from, and natural convection around, a refrigerant mass such as water ice, dry ice, gel packs or sealed cassettes charged with a phase-change material.
2	
3	Passive carriers are attractive because they have no battery to charge, no motor to fail and no electrical approval burden for air transport. They are also harder to control. When a refrigerant mass is simply laid on top of, beside or beneath a payload, the cooled air falls where gravity and the packing arrangement happen to send it. Items directly against the refrigerant are driven toward the cold end of the acceptable band or below it, while items on the far side of the payload sit in a stagnant warm layer. The result is a temperature spread across the payload that grows as the load is packed more densely, and that varies from shipment to shipment because it depends on how a particular packer arranged the goods and the refrigerant on a particular day.
4	
5	Attempts to impose a defined circulation path on a passive carrier run into a practical difficulty. The path is defined by clearances, by openings and by the alignment between them, and every one of those relationships is destroyed if the component that carries the openings is set down rotated, offset or skewed by a person working quickly at a packing bench. A carrier that circulates air well when it is assembled precisely, and poorly when it is not, delivers the variability it was intended to remove. Packing instructions, printed arrows and keyed corner blocks all depend on the packer looking, and none of them acts on a component that has already been set down out of position.
6	
7	Two further problems attend repeated reuse of a passive carrier. First, moist ambient air admitted each time the carrier is opened condenses on the cold surfaces of the refrigerant mass and runs down into the payload space, wetting labels and cartons and, over many cycles, leaving standing water in the base of the carrier. Where the refrigerant is a sealed cassette, drying the interior often means removing the cassette from service. Second, a passive carrier gives no account of itself. If the payload was exposed to a temperature excursion in transit, and the refrigerant has since recovered, an inspection at the receiving dock shows a cold carrier and a firm cassette, and the excursion leaves no trace. Electronic data loggers record such events but add cost, battery management and a reading step to every unit shipped, and they report a sensor location rather than the state of the refrigerant that the payload actually depends on.
8	
9	There remains a need for a reusable passive carrier that establishes the same circulation path around the payload every time it is closed, without a powered air mover and without relying on the care of the person who packed it, that manages the condensate produced by repeated opening without taking the refrigerant out of service, and that retains a visible mechanical record of a refrigerant temperature excursion after the refrigerant has recovered.
10

25	The same closing movement retains the thermal module 40. Ledges 18 project inward from the side walls 14 of the outer shell 10 beneath the resilient feet 58 of the spacer frame 42, as seen in FIG. 3, and closure of the insulated lid 60 presses the resilient feet 58 against the ledges 18. 28

The rising stream divides along the confronting inner faces of the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46, giving two cooling streams that travel outward over the cassette faces. Because the supply and return legs are separated by the tray side walls 26 rather than sharing one opening, the descending cold stream is not obliged to pass through the ascending warm stream, and the payload is swept along its length rather than chilled at the surface nearest a refrigerant mass. A saturated wick is therefore drawn out and replaced as a service item between shipments, by lifting out the product tray 20 and pulling the pull tab 74, without opening a phase-change cassette and without taking the cassettes out of service to dry the interior. 40	
41	Referring to FIG. 5, the outer shell 10 carries a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside the carrier 100. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 includes a body received in the outer shell 10, an indicator stem 82 movable in the body between a stowed position and an exposed position, a temperature-responsive latch 84 that retains the indicator stem 82 in the stowed position, and a spring 86 biasing the indicator stem 82 toward the exposed position. The body of the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is seated in a bore through a wall of the outer shell 10 and has an internal shoulder, the spring 86 acting between that internal shoulder and a collar on the indicator stem 82, and the temperature-responsive latch 84 being carried by the body and engaging the indicator stem 82. The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44, an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 lying against or in conductive contact with the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position.

43	The temperature-responsive latch 84 is arranged to release when the first phase-change cassette 44 softens, that is, when the phase-change material of that cassette has passed out of the state in which it holds the payload at temperature. In some implementations the exposed position is one in which an outer end portion of the indicator stem 82 projects beyond an outer surface of the outer shell 10; in others it is one in which a contrasting portion of the indicator stem 82 is presented at the outer surface.

The indication is produced by the state of the refrigerant on which the payload depends rather than by a sensor at an arbitrary point in the air space, and requires no battery, no reading device and no data transfer.
46	
47	The mechanical exposure indicator 80 does not control airflow. It neither opens, closes nor throttles the central inlet opening 48, the guide ducts 50, the peripheral outlet openings 54, the side supply passages 28, the perforations 30 or the lower return passage 24, and the circulation path is the same whether or not the mechanical exposure indicator 80 has moved to the exposed position. 49	Operation
50	
51	In use, phase-change cassettes conditioned to the temperature required by the payload are fitted to the spacer frame 42 as the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46. Goods are placed in the product tray 20 and the product tray 20 is placed in the outer shell 10 so that the tray feet 22 stand on the floor 12, leaving the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20 and the two side supply passages 28 between the tray side walls 26 and the side walls 14. Air thereafter circulates along the circulation path without operation of any powered air mover. At the destination, the insulated lid 60 is opened, the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is read and, if it stands in the exposed position, reset manually, the product tray 20 is lifted out with the goods, and the absorbent wick 72 is drawn out by the pull tab 74 and replaced if saturated.

53	Alternatives
54	
55	The number of phase-change cassettes held by the spacer frame 42 is two in the described arrangement, the two being opposed across the central space so that each face of the rising stream is cooled symmetrically. The mating channel 56 and the depending indexing rib 62 may be interchanged in the sense that the channel may be longer than the rib or the rib longer than the channel, provided that entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position. The peripheral outlet openings 54 may be continuous slots along the outboard lower regions of the spacer frame 42 or a series of discrete openings, provided that they overlap the side supply passages 28 in the registered position. 56	
57	The described implementations are examples. A person skilled in the art may combine, substitute or omit the described features within the scope of the claims that follow.

In the following description, directional terms such as upper, lower, above, below, inward and outward refer to the carrier in its normal upright orientation with the insulated lid uppermost. The same reference numeral denotes the same part throughout the drawings.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a passive cold-chain carrier 100 includes an insulated outer shell 10, a product tray 20 removably received in the outer shell 10, a thermal module 40 removably received in the outer shell 10 above the product tray 20, and an insulated lid 60 closable on an upper edge of the outer shell 10. The outer shell 10 has a floor 12 and side walls 14 that rise from the floor 12 and bound an interior of the outer shell 10. The outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are formed of thermally insulating material such as moulded expanded polymer, a vacuum insulated panel assembly, a rigid polyurethane foam core within a moulded skin, or a combination of these. The carrier 100 is reusable, the product tray 20 and the thermal module 40 being liftable out of the outer shell 10 for loading, cleaning and reconditioning.

The product tray 20 is an upwardly open receptacle having a bottom wall and tray side walls 26, and receives the goods to be transported. A product region is the space within the product tray 20 that is occupied by those goods. Tray feet 22 depend from the product tray 20 and stand on the floor 12, so that the product tray 20 is supported above the floor 12 and a lower return passage 24 remains between the bottom wall of the product tray 20 and the floor 12. The tray feet 22 may be integrally moulded projections, separate ribs, or a pedestal frame, and are of sufficient number and footprint to carry a loaded tray without collapsing the lower return passage 24.

The tray side walls 26 are spaced inward from the side walls 14 of the outer shell 10, so that two side supply passages 28 are formed, each side supply passage 28 extending downward between one tray side wall 26 and the confronting side wall 14. Perforations 30 through the product tray 20 open from the side supply passages 28 into the product region and into the lower return passage 24. The tray side walls 26, one side supply passage 28 and the perforations 30 are seen in FIG. 4. The perforations 30 may be formed in a lower portion of the tray side walls 26, in the bottom wall of the product tray 20, or in both, and may be round holes, slots, or a louvered pattern. In each case the perforations 30 are distributed along the length of the product tray 20 so that air delivered by the side supply passages 28 enters the product region along that length rather than at a single point.

The thermal module

Referring to FIG. 2, the thermal module 40 includes a rigid spacer frame 42 and two opposed phase-change cassettes held by the spacer frame 42, namely a first phase-change cassette 44 and a second phase-change cassette 46. Each phase-change cassette is a sealed rigid container charged with a phase-change material, and the two cassettes are held by the spacer frame 42 in an upright, mutually facing arrangement so that an inner face of the first phase-change cassette 44 confronts an inner face of the second phase-change cassette 46 across a central space of the spacer frame 42. The phase-change cassettes are removable from the spacer frame 42 so that cassettes conditioned to the temperature required by a given payload can be fitted before packing and exchanged between shipments.

The spacer frame 42 defines a central inlet opening 48 that opens downward into the central space between the two phase-change cassettes, so that air rising from the product region enters the central space between the confronting inner faces. The spacer frame 42 further defines two downward guide ducts 50, seen in FIG. 4, located beside the phase-change cassettes, each guide duct 50 lying outboard of an outer face of one of the phase-change cassettes, and peripheral outlet openings 54 at lower outboard regions of the spacer frame 42, each peripheral outlet opening 54 being at a lower end of one of the guide ducts 50. The spacer frame 42 holds the phase-change cassettes clear of the product tray 20, so that goods in the product region are not in contact with a cassette surface and are cooled by the circulating air rather than by direct contact.

The spacer frame 42 also defines a mating channel 56 that opens upward at a top region of the spacer frame 42, and carries resilient feet 58 at lower outboard regions of the spacer frame 42. The mating channel 56 and a rib entering it from above are shaped so that engagement between them during the closing travel translates the spacer frame 42 horizontally into position, rather than merely resting one upon the other. The resilient feet 58 may be elastomeric pads, moulded spring tabs, or compressible polymer blocks.

Registration and retention by the lid

The insulated lid 60 carries a depending indexing rib 62 on an underside of the insulated lid 60, and a compressible lid gasket 64 that extends around the underside of the insulated lid 60 outboard of the depending indexing rib 62. The depending indexing rib 62, the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and the compressible lid gasket 64 are seen in FIG. 3. As the insulated lid 60 is closed, the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 56 of the spacer frame 42 and shifts the thermal module 40 into a registered position in which the peripheral outlet openings 54 overlap the side supply passages 28. The engagement is progressive: the depending indexing rib 62 first meets the mating channel 56 while the lid is still spaced above the outer shell 10, and the remaining closing travel translates the spacer frame 42 horizontally until the mating channel 56 is seated on the depending indexing rib 62.

This sequence addresses the practical problem that the circulation path depends on an alignment which a person packing quickly at a bench cannot be relied upon to produce. The thermal module 40 need only be dropped into the outer shell 10 approximately, and may be set down offset or skewed within the clearance available to it. The alignment on which the circulation path depends is then created by closing the lid, which is an act the packer cannot omit, because a carrier that is not closed does not ship. The compressible lid gasket 64 bears against the upper edge of the outer shell 10 and is compressed only at the end of the closing travel, after the depending indexing rib 62 has completed registration, so that the carrier cannot be sealed shut around a thermal module 40 that is still out of position.

The same closing movement retains the thermal module 40. Ledges 18 project inward from the side walls 14 of the outer shell 10 beneath the resilient feet 58 of the spacer frame 42, as seen in FIG. 3, and closure of the insulated lid 60 presses the resilient feet 58 against the ledges 18. The resilient feet 58 are compressed between the ledges 18 and the load path from the insulated lid 60, so that the thermal module 40 is held down and cannot lift away from the product tray 20 during transport. Retention by compression of resilient members accommodates the tolerance stack of moulded insulating parts, and maintains a downward holding force as the carrier is jolted or inverted, so the registered overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 54 and the side supply passages 28 that was established at closure persists through the journey.

The circulation path

In the registered position, the outer shell 10, the product tray 20, the thermal module 40 and the insulated lid 60 cooperate to define a circulation path. Air warmed by the goods rises from the product region within the product tray 20 and enters the central inlet opening 48. The rising stream divides along the confronting inner faces of the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46, giving two cooling streams that travel outward over the cassette faces. Each cooled stream descends through one of the guide ducts 50 beside the phase-change cassettes, leaves the thermal module 40 through the peripheral outlet openings 54, and enters the side supply passage 28 registered beneath that peripheral outlet opening 54. Each descending stream then passes through the perforations 30 in the product tray 20 and returns through the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20, from which it rises again through the product region.

The carrier 100 is free of a fan, a pump and any powered air mover. Circulation is driven by the density difference between air warmed in the product region and air cooled along the faces of the phase-change cassettes. The geometry supports that difference rather than substituting for it: the cooled air is produced at the top of the carrier and is given a continuous downward path of its own along the guide ducts 50 and the side supply passages 28, while the warmed air is given a continuous upward path through the product region to the central inlet opening 48, and the two paths meet only at the central inlet opening 48 and beneath the product tray 20. Because the supply and return legs are separated by the tray side walls 26 rather than sharing one opening, the descending cold stream is not obliged to pass through the ascending warm stream, and the payload is swept along its length rather than chilled at the surface nearest a refrigerant mass. The lower return passage 24 also keeps the coldest returning air off the goods until it has mixed, so that goods at the bottom of the product tray 20 are not driven below the temperature band.

Condensate management

A condensate channel 70 is a shallow upwardly open trough that extends around the product tray 20 at a lower region of the outer shell 10, beneath the side supply passages 28. A removable absorbent wick 72 lies in the condensate channel 70. Discharge openings 76 at lower ends of the guide ducts 50 discharge condensate into the condensate channel 70. The condensate channel 70, the absorbent wick 72, the pull tab 74 described below, one discharge opening 76 and the lower end of one guide duct 50 are seen in FIG. 4. Moist ambient air admitted whenever the carrier is opened condenses on the cold cassette surfaces and on the walls of the guide ducts 50, and the resulting water runs down the guide ducts 50 and is delivered through the discharge openings 76 to the condensate channel 70 rather than onto the goods.

The absorbent wick 72 carries a pull tab 74 that remains accessible when the product tray 20 is removed from the outer shell 10. A saturated wick is therefore drawn out and replaced as a service item between shipments, by lifting out the product tray 20 and pulling the pull tab 74, without opening a phase-change cassette and without taking the cassettes out of service to dry the interior. The absorbent wick 72 may be a cellulose or polymer fibre strip, a superabsorbent polymer sleeve, or a moulded absorbent ring shaped to the condensate channel 70.

Mechanical exposure indicator

Referring to FIG. 5, the outer shell 10 carries a mechanical exposure indicator 80 visible from outside the carrier 100. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 includes a body received in the outer shell 10, an indicator stem 82 movable in the body between a stowed position and an exposed position, a temperature-responsive latch 84 that retains the indicator stem 82 in the stowed position, and a spring 86 biasing the indicator stem 82 toward the exposed position. The body of the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is seated in a bore through a wall of the outer shell 10 and has an internal shoulder, the spring 86 acting between that internal shoulder and a collar on the indicator stem 82, and the temperature-responsive latch 84 being carried by the body and engaging the indicator stem 82. The indicator stem 82 is thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44, an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 lying against or in conductive contact with the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position.

The temperature-responsive latch 84 is arranged to release when the first phase-change cassette 44 softens, that is, when the phase-change material of that cassette has passed out of the state in which it holds the payload at temperature. On release, the spring 86 moves the indicator stem 82 to the exposed position, in which the indicator stem 82 is visible from outside the outer shell 10. In some implementations the exposed position is one in which an outer end portion of the indicator stem 82 projects beyond an outer surface of the outer shell 10; in others it is one in which a contrasting portion of the indicator stem 82 is presented at the outer surface.

The exposed position is a latched position. The mechanical exposure indicator 80 retains the indicator stem 82 in the exposed position after the first phase-change cassette 44 has cooled again and the temperature-responsive latch 84 has returned to its retaining condition, and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is reset manually only after the carrier 100 is opened. A receiving inspection therefore sees the excursion even though the carrier presents itself as cold and the cassette as firm, and the record cannot be erased in transit by the cassette recovering. The indication is produced by the state of the refrigerant on which the payload depends rather than by a sensor at an arbitrary point in the air space, and requires no battery, no reading device and no data transfer.

The mechanical exposure indicator 80 does not control airflow. It neither opens, closes nor throttles the central inlet opening 48, the guide ducts 50, the peripheral outlet openings 54, the side supply passages 28, the perforations 30 or the lower return passage 24, and the circulation path is the same whether or not the mechanical exposure indicator 80 has moved to the exposed position. The behaviour of the carrier 100 is therefore unchanged by the act of reporting, and a tripped indicator does not degrade the protection given to the payload for the remainder of the journey.

Operation

In use, phase-change cassettes conditioned to the temperature required by the payload are fitted to the spacer frame 42 as the first phase-change cassette 44 and the second phase-change cassette 46. Goods are placed in the product tray 20 and the product tray 20 is placed in the outer shell 10 so that the tray feet 22 stand on the floor 12, leaving the lower return passage 24 beneath the product tray 20 and the two side supply passages 28 between the tray side walls 26 and the side walls 14. The thermal module 40 is placed in the outer shell 10 above the product tray 20. The insulated lid 60 is then closed, whereby the depending indexing rib 62 enters the mating channel 56 and shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position, the resilient feet 58 are pressed against the ledges 18 to retain the thermal module 40, and the compressible lid gasket 64 seals against the upper edge of the outer shell 10. Air thereafter circulates along the circulation path without operation of any powered air mover. At the destination, the insulated lid 60 is opened, the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is read and, if it stands in the exposed position, reset manually, the product tray 20 is lifted out with the goods, and the absorbent wick 72 is drawn out by the pull tab 74 and replaced if saturated.

Alternatives

The number of phase-change cassettes held by the spacer frame 42 is two in the described arrangement, the two being opposed across the central space so that each face of the rising stream is cooled symmetrically. The mating channel 56 and the depending indexing rib 62 may be interchanged in the sense that the channel may be longer than the rib or the rib longer than the channel, provided that entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position. The peripheral outlet openings 54 may be continuous slots along the outboard lower regions of the spacer frame 42 or a series of discrete openings, provided that they overlap the side supply passages 28 in the registered position. The condensate channel 70, the absorbent wick 72, the pull tab 74, the discharge openings 76 and the mechanical exposure indicator 80 are optional features, and a carrier 100 may be built with the registered circulation path and the lid-driven registration alone, or with any combination of the optional features.

The described implementations are examples. A person skilled in the art may combine, substitute or omit the described features within the scope of the claims that follow.

input.summary:
Preflight source-fidelity review of the p10 draft against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to the disclosure). input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, priority and government-support formalities.

Core coverage is good: the shell/tray/module/lid architecture, tray feet and lower return passage, side supply passages, spacer frame with two opposed cassettes, central inlet, guide ducts, peripheral outlet openings, the full circulation loop, the "no fan, pump or powered air mover" limitation, lid rib / mating channel registration, gasket-after-registration sequencing, resilient feet on ledges, the wick/condensate channel/pull tab, and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator all trace to exact inventor sentences. Independent claims 1, 16 and 20 are fully traceable, as are dependent claims 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 23. The abstract (141 words) matches claim 1. numerals.md is complete and one-to-one with the description; no drafting notes, placeholders or open questions remain anywhere in draft/ or figures/.

24 findings are reported. The critical ones are untraced technical matter:

1. Material and construction menus invented by the drafter — insulating materials for shell and lid ("moulded expanded polymer, a vacuum insulated panel assembly, a rigid polyurethane foam core within a moulded skin"), tray-foot forms, resilient-foot materials, wick materials, and perforation forms. The disclosure names none of these; it says only "insulated outer shell", "feet", "resilient feet", "absorbent wick", "perforations".

2. Cassette internal construction ("a sealed rigid container charged with a phase-change material") — the disclosure says only "phase-change cassettes".

3. A new non-contact cooling relationship — "The spacer frame 42 holds the phase-change cassettes clear of the product tray 20, so that goods ... are not in contact with a cassette surface" — carried into claim 6. The disclosure says only that the frame "rests above the product tray".

4. Perforation placement, and distribution "along the length of the product tray", carried into claim 7. The disclosure says only "perforations in the product tray".

5. The entire internal mechanism of the exposure indicator — body seated in a bore, stepped bore with an internal shoulder, a collar on the stem, a coil spring between shoulder and collar, a latch block in a recess — appearing in both the description and fig-05.md. The disclosure gives only stem, temperature-responsive latch and spring.

6. Narrowing "thermally coupled" into "conductive contact" with the cassette (description and claim 14).

7. Two alternative exposed-position embodiments (projecting stem vs. contrasting portion at the outer surface), and two Alternatives-section variants (rib/channel relative length; peripheral outlets as continuous slots or discrete openings) with no inventor basis.

8. Asserted performance results not in the disclosure: "keeps the coldest returning air off the goods until it has mixed, so that goods at the bottom ... are not driven below the temperature band", and "accommodates the tolerance stack of moulded insulating parts".

9. Figure-brief substance beyond depiction convention: fig-02 states spacer-frame proportions ("longer from left to right than it is deep ... lower in height than it is deep") and a count of four resilient feet; fig-03 makes the indexing rib "an integral part" of the lid.

Verified internal inconsistencies:

- The description contradicts itself and claim 1 on where the perforations deliver air: paragraph 9 has them opening "into the product region" along the tray length, while paragraph 29, claim 1, claim 20 and the disclosure route the descending stream through the perforations into the lower return passage before it rises through the product region.
- Peripheral outlet openings 54 and discharge openings 76 are both recited "at lower ends of the guide ducts" (claims 1/9 and 16/19, and the description) with nothing distinguishing them.
- fig-01 opens each guide duct downward above the side gap; fig-02 puts the peripheral outlet openings through the long side wall; fig-04 shows only the condensate discharge opening at the duct's lower end, leaving the air outlet undepicted.
- fig-01 has the lid underside "contacting" the tops of both shell walls, while fig-03 shows the compressed gasket between those same surfaces.
- fig-05 shows the stem's inner end contacting cassette 44 directly across open space, which cannot coexist with fig-02 and the description, where a guide duct and the frame's outboard wall lie between each cassette and the shell wall.
- fig-01 places 10 and 100 on the same shell body.

Formalities: FIGS. 1, 3, 4 and 5 are sectional views with no section line and no source view designating the cutting plane, and FIGS. 3-5 are not tied to FIG. 1; the title departs from the brief's working title; claim 21 and the Brief Description say "lid gasket" where the description and numerals say "compressible lid gasket 64".

No patentability, novelty, validity or prior-art-tracing assessment was performed, and rendered images were not inspected.

findings.title: Insulating materials for the shell and lid are invented by the drafter
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Overall arrangement", paragraph beginning "Referring to FIG. 1"
findings.detail: The description recites a menu of construction materials for the outer shell and lid. The disclosure never names any material for any part of the carrier; it says only that the shell and lid are insulated. No affirmative inventor passage exists for expanded polymer, vacuum insulated panels, or a polyurethane foam core in a moulded skin.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are formed of thermally insulating material such as moulded expanded polymer, a vacuum insulated panel assembly, a rigid polyurethane foam core within a moulded skin, or a combination of these." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 5): "A reusable passive cold-chain carrier has an insulated outer shell, a removable product tray, a removable thermal module, and an insulated lid." — no material is named anywhere in the disclosure.
findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The outer shell 10 and the insulated lid 60 are formed of thermally insulating material."

findings.title: Tray-foot forms, number and footprint are unsupported
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Overall arrangement", paragraph beginning "The product tray 20 is an upwardly open receptacle"
findings.detail: The description adds three structural alternatives for the tray feet plus a requirement as to their number and footprint. The disclosure says only that the tray is suspended above the floor by feet.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The tray feet 22 may be integrally moulded projections, separate ribs, or a pedestal frame, and are of sufficient number and footprint to carry a loaded tray without collapsing the lower return passage 24." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 5): "The product tray is suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray." — no form, count or footprint is disclosed.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The tray feet 22 may be integrally moulded projections, separate ribs, or a pedestal frame, and are of sufficient number and footprint to carry a loaded tray without collapsing the lower return passage 24."

findings.title: Perforation location, shape and lengthwise distribution are unsupported, in the description and in claim 7
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Overall arrangement", final paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 7
findings.detail: The description assigns the perforations to specific walls and gives three hole geometries and a distribution requirement, and claim 7 claims that location and distribution as a dependent limitation. The disclosure locates the perforations only "in the product tray" and says nothing about their shape, wall, or distribution.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "The perforations 30 may be formed in a lower portion of the tray side walls 26, in the bottom wall of the product tray 20, or in both, and may be round holes, slots, or a louvered pattern. In each case the perforations 30 are distributed along the length of the product tray 20 so that air delivered by the side supply passages 28 enters the product region along that length rather than at a single point." Candidate (claim 7): "wherein the perforations are formed in a lower portion of the tray side walls and are distributed along a length of the product tray." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 7): "enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage."
findings.fix: Delete both quoted description sentences, and cancel claim 7, renumbering claims 8-23 as 7-22 and updating the dependencies in claims 9, 10 (from claim 8 to claim 7) and 21, 22, 23 (from claim 20 to claim 19) accordingly.

findings.title: Cassette internal construction ("sealed rigid container charged with a phase-change material") is unsupported
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The thermal module", first paragraph
findings.detail: The description specifies the construction of each cassette. The disclosure refers only to "phase-change cassettes" and never states that a cassette is a rigid container, that it is sealed, or how it is charged.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "Each phase-change cassette is a sealed rigid container charged with a phase-change material". Nearest source (disclosure.md line 7): "The thermal module is a rigid spacer frame holding two opposed phase-change cassettes." — rigidity is attributed to the spacer frame, not to the cassettes, and no container construction is disclosed.
findings.fix: Replace the clause with: "Each phase-change cassette holds a phase-change material".

findings.title: "Holds the cassettes clear of the product tray" / no-contact cooling relationship is unsupported, in the description and in claim 6
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The thermal module", second paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 6
findings.detail: The description and claim 6 add a spatial relationship (cassettes held clear of the tray) and a resulting functional limitation (goods not in contact with a cassette surface, cooled by air rather than contact). The disclosure states only that the spacer frame rests above the product tray and below the lid; it never says the cassettes are held clear of the tray, nor that goods do not contact a cassette.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "The spacer frame 42 holds the phase-change cassettes clear of the product tray 20, so that goods in the product region are not in contact with a cassette surface and are cooled by the circulating air rather than by direct contact." Candidate (claim 6): "the spacer frame holds the phase-change cassettes clear of the product tray so that goods in the product region are cooled by air of the circulation path rather than by contact with a phase-change cassette." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 7): "The spacer frame rests above the product tray and below the lid."
findings.fix: Delete the quoted description sentence, and amend claim 6 to read: "The passive cold-chain carrier of claim 1, wherein the phase-change cassettes are removable from the spacer frame."

findings.title: Resilient-foot material alternatives are unsupported
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The thermal module", third paragraph
findings.detail: Three constructions are offered for the resilient feet. The disclosure names only "resilient feet of the spacer frame" and says nothing about what they are made of or how they are formed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The resilient feet 58 may be elastomeric pads, moulded spring tabs, or compressible polymer blocks." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 9): "The same closing movement presses resilient feet of the spacer frame against ledges of the shell so that the module cannot lift away from the tray during transport."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The resilient feet 58 may be elastomeric pads, moulded spring tabs, or compressible polymer blocks."

findings.title: Absorbent-wick material alternatives are unsupported
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Condensate management", final paragraph
findings.detail: Three wick constructions are offered. The disclosure identifies the part only as "a removable absorbent wick" and gives no material, form or shape.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The absorbent wick 72 may be a cellulose or polymer fibre strip, a superabsorbent polymer sleeve, or a moulded absorbent ring shaped to the condensate channel 70." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 11): "A removable absorbent wick lies in a shallow condensate channel around the product tray."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The absorbent wick 72 may be a cellulose or polymer fibre strip, a superabsorbent polymer sleeve, or a moulded absorbent ring shaped to the condensate channel 70."

findings.title: Internal mechanism of the exposure indicator (body, bore, stepped shoulder, collar) is invented
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator", first paragraph; figures/fig-05.md, "Geometry to draw"
findings.detail: The description and the FIG. 5 brief specify an indicator body seated in a bore through the shell wall, a bore that is stepped to form an internal shoulder, a collar on the stem, a coil spring acting between shoulder and collar, and a latch block seated in a recess in the body. The disclosure discloses only three elements — an indicator stem, a temperature-responsive latch, and a spring — plus the fact that the indicator is carried by the shell and visible from outside. None of the connecting structure has any inventor basis.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "The body of the mechanical exposure indicator 80 is seated in a bore through a wall of the outer shell 10 and has an internal shoulder, the spring 86 acting between that internal shoulder and a collar on the indicator stem 82, and the temperature-responsive latch 84 being carried by the body and engaging the indicator stem 82." Candidate (fig-05.md): "Its bore is wider at the part nearer the inner surface than at the part nearer the outer surface, the step between the two widths forming an internal shoulder facing left"; "A collar is drawn on the shaft within the wider part of the bore, standing proud of the shaft all round"; "A small block sits in a recess in the hatched upper wall of the tubular body". Nearest source (disclosure.md line 13): "An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch. If that cassette softens enough to release the latch, a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position."
findings.fix: Delete the quoted description sentence. In fig-05.md, delete the stepped-bore/internal-shoulder sentence, the collar sentence and the words "in a recess", and revise the spring paragraph to read: "A coil spring surrounds the shaft within the tubular body, drawn as aligned loops and shown compressed. This spring is the spring 86." Keep only stem 82, latch 84 and spring 86 as the indicator elements, with the indicator 80 shown schematically as a body carried by the shell wall.

findings.title: "Conductive contact" narrows the disclosed "thermally coupled" without support (description, claim 14, FIG. 5)
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator", first paragraph; draft/09-claims.md claim 14; figures/fig-05.md
findings.detail: The disclosure states only that the indicator stem is "thermally coupled" to one cassette. The draft converts this into physical abutment/conductive contact in the description, claims it in claim 14, and draws it in FIG. 5. Contact is a different and narrower relationship than thermal coupling and has no affirmative inventor passage.
findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 lying against or in conductive contact with the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position." Candidate (claim 14): "wherein an inner end region of the indicator stem lies in conductive contact with said one of the phase-change cassettes when the thermal module is in the registered position." Candidate (fig-05.md): "its left face confronting and contacting the inner end of the shaft." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 13): "An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch."
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted clause with "an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 being thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position". Cancel claim 14 and renumber the following claims. In fig-05.md, replace "its left face confronting and contacting the inner end of the shaft" with "its left face confronting the inner end of the shaft".

findings.title: Two alternative forms of the exposed position are unsupported embodiments
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator", second paragraph
findings.detail: The description offers two alternative implementations of what the exposed position looks like. The disclosure says only that the indicator is "visible from outside" and that the spring moves the stem "to a latched exposed position"; neither a projecting stem end nor a contrasting portion presented at the surface is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "In some implementations the exposed position is one in which an outer end portion of the indicator stem 82 projects beyond an outer surface of the outer shell 10; in others it is one in which a contrasting portion of the indicator stem 82 is presented at the outer surface." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 13): "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. ... a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence beginning "In some implementations the exposed position is one in which ..." and rely on the preceding sentence, "the indicator stem 82 is visible from outside the outer shell 10."

findings.title: Alternatives section adds an unsupported rib/channel length variant
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Alternatives", second sentence
findings.detail: The description offers a variant in which the relative lengths of the mating channel and the indexing rib are interchanged. The disclosure describes only one arrangement: the lid carries a depending rib that enters a mating channel in the spacer frame. No relative-length variant is disclosed. (The sentence is also internally confused: it announces an interchange of the two parts but then describes only their relative length.)
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The mating channel 56 and the depending indexing rib 62 may be interchanged in the sense that the channel may be longer than the rib or the rib longer than the channel, provided that entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 9): "The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position".
findings.fix: Delete the sentence and, if a general statement is wanted, retain only: "Entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position."

findings.title: Alternatives section adds unsupported forms of the peripheral outlet openings
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Alternatives", third sentence
findings.detail: Continuous slots and discrete openings are offered as alternative forms of the peripheral outlet openings. The disclosure recites only "peripheral outlet openings aligned with the side supply passages" and gives no geometry.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The peripheral outlet openings 54 may be continuous slots along the outboard lower regions of the spacer frame 42 or a series of discrete openings, provided that they overlap the side supply passages 28 in the registered position." data.summary:
Preflight source-fidelity review of the p10 draft against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is verbatim identical to the disclosure). input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, priority and government-support formalities.

Core coverage is good: the shell/tray/module/lid architecture, tray feet and lower return passage, side supply passages, spacer frame with two opposed cassettes, central inlet, guide ducts, peripheral outlet openings, the full circulation loop, the "no fan, pump or powered air mover" limitation, lid rib / mating channel registration, gasket-after-registration sequencing, resilient feet on ledges, the wick/condensate channel/pull tab, and the irreversible mechanical exposure indicator all trace to exact inventor sentences. Independent claims 1, 16 and 20 are fully traceable, as are dependent claims 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 17, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 23. The abstract (141 words) matches claim 1. numerals.md is complete and one-to-one with the description; no drafting notes, placeholders or open questions remain anywhere in draft/ or figures/.

24 findings are reported. The critical ones are untraced technical matter:

1. Material and construction menus invented by the drafter — insulating materials for shell and lid ("moulded expanded polymer, a vacuum insulated panel assembly, a rigid polyurethane foam core within a moulded skin"), tray-foot forms, resilient-foot materials, wick materials, and perforation forms. The disclosure names none of these; it says only "insulated outer shell", "feet", "resilient feet", "absorbent wick", "perforations".

2. Cassette internal construction ("a sealed rigid container charged with a phase-change material") — the disclosure says only "phase-change cassettes".

3. A new non-contact cooling relationship — "The spacer frame 42 holds the phase-change cassettes clear of the product tray 20, so that goods ... are not in contact with a cassette surface" — carried into claim 6. The disclosure says only that the frame "rests above the product tray".

4. Perforation placement, and distribution "along the length of the product tray", carried into claim 7. The disclosure says only "perforations in the product tray".

5. The entire internal mechanism of the exposure indicator — body seated in a bore, stepped bore with an internal shoulder, a collar on the stem, a coil spring between shoulder and collar, a latch block in a recess — appearing in both the description and fig-05.md. The disclosure gives only stem, temperature-responsive latch and spring.

6. Narrowing "thermally coupled" into "conductive contact" with the cassette (description and claim 14).

7. Two alternative exposed-position embodiments (projecting stem vs. contrasting portion at the outer surface), and two Alternatives-section variants (rib/channel relative length; peripheral outlets as continuous slots or discrete openings) with no inventor basis.

8. Asserted performance results not in the disclosure: "keeps the coldest returning air off the goods until it has mixed, so that goods at the bottom ... are not driven below the temperature band", and "accommodates the tolerance stack of moulded insulating parts".

9. Figure-brief substance beyond depiction convention: fig-02 states spacer-frame proportions ("longer from left to right than it is deep ... lower in height than it is deep") and a count of four resilient feet; fig-03 makes the indexing rib "an integral part" of the lid.

Verified internal inconsistencies:

- The description contradicts itself and claim 1 on where the perforations deliver air: paragraph 9 has them opening "into the product region" along the tray length, while paragraph 29, claim 1, claim 20 and the disclosure route the descending stream through the perforations into the lower return passage before it rises through the product region.
- Peripheral outlet openings 54 and discharge openings 76 are both recited "at lower ends of the guide ducts" (claims 1/9 and 16/19, and the description) with nothing distinguishing them.
- fig-01 opens each guide duct downward above the side gap; fig-02 puts the peripheral outlet openings through the long side wall; fig-04 shows only the condensate discharge opening at the duct's lower end, leaving the air outlet undepicted.
- fig-01 has the lid underside "contacting" the tops of both shell walls, while fig-03 shows the compressed gasket between those same surfaces.
- fig-05 shows the stem's inner end contacting cassette 44 directly across open space, which cannot coexist with fig-02 and the description, where a guide duct and the frame's outboard wall lie between each cassette and the shell wall.
- fig-01 places 10 and 100 on the same shell body.

Formalities: FIGS. 1, 3, 4 and 5 are sectional views with no section line and no source view designating the cutting plane, and FIGS. 3-5 are not tied to FIG. 1; the title departs from the brief's working title; claim 21 and the Brief Description say "lid gasket" where the description and numerals say "compressible lid gasket 64".

No patentability, novelty, validity or prior-art-tracing assessment was performed, and rendered images were not inspected.

findings.title: Insulating materials for the shell and lid are invented by the drafter

findings.detail: The description and the FIG. 5 brief specify an indicator body seated in a bore through the shell wall, a bore that is stepped to form an internal shoulder, a collar on the stem, a coil spring acting between shoulder and collar, and a latch block seated in a recess in the body. findings.evidence: Candidate (description): "an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 lying against or in conductive contact with the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position." Candidate (claim 14): "wherein an inner end region of the indicator stem lies in conductive contact with said one of the phase-change cassettes when the thermal module is in the registered position." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 13): "An indicator stem is thermally coupled to one phase-change cassette and retained by a temperature-responsive latch."
findings.fix: In the description, replace the quoted clause with "an inner end region of the indicator stem 82 being thermally coupled to the first phase-change cassette 44 when the thermal module 40 is in the registered position". In fig-05.md, replace "its left face confronting and contacting the inner end of the shaft" with "its left face confronting the inner end of the shaft".

findings.title: Two alternative forms of the exposed position are unsupported embodiments
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Mechanical exposure indicator", second paragraph
findings.detail: The description offers two alternative implementations of what the exposed position looks like. The disclosure says only that the indicator is "visible from outside" and that the spring moves the stem "to a latched exposed position"; neither a projecting stem end nor a contrasting portion presented at the surface is disclosed.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "In some implementations the exposed position is one in which an outer end portion of the indicator stem 82 projects beyond an outer surface of the outer shell 10; in others it is one in which a contrasting portion of the indicator stem 82 is presented at the outer surface." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 13): "The shell includes a mechanical exposure indicator visible from outside. ... a spring moves the indicator stem to a latched exposed position."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence beginning "In some implementations the exposed position is one in which ..." and rely on the preceding sentence, "the indicator stem 82 is visible from outside the outer shell 10."

findings.title: Alternatives section adds an unsupported rib/channel length variant
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Alternatives", second sentence
findings.detail: The description offers a variant in which the relative lengths of the mating channel and the indexing rib are interchanged. findings.evidence: Candidate: "The mating channel 56 and the depending indexing rib 62 may be interchanged in the sense that the channel may be longer than the rib or the rib longer than the channel, provided that entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 9): "The lid carries a depending indexing rib. As the lid closes, the rib enters a mating channel in the spacer frame and shifts the thermal module into a registered position".
findings.fix: Delete the sentence and, if a general statement is wanted, retain only: "Entry of the depending indexing rib 62 into the mating channel 56 during closing travel shifts the thermal module 40 into the registered position."

findings.title: Asserted thermal result about the lower return passage has no inventor basis
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The circulation path", final sentence
findings.detail: The description asserts a specific performance result of the lower return passage — mixing of the coldest returning air and prevention of under-temperature at the bottom of the tray. The disclosure describes the lower return passage only as a geometric passage in the flow loop and states no such effect.
findings.evidence: Candidate: "The lower return passage 24 also keeps the coldest returning air off the goods until it has mixed, so that goods at the bottom of the product tray 20 are not driven below the temperature band." Nearest source (disclosure.md line 5, 7): "The product tray is suspended above the shell floor by feet so that a lower return passage remains under the tray." / "... and returns through the lower return passage."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence "The lower return passage 24 also keeps the coldest returning air off the goods until it has mixed, so that goods at the bottom of the product tray 20 are not driven below the temperature band."

findings.title: "Tolerance stack of moulded insulating parts" result is unsupported and reintroduces an undisclosed material

findings.evidence: Candidate: "Retention by compression of resilient members accommodates the tolerance stack of moulded insulating parts, and maintains a downward holding force as the carrier is jolted or inverted, so the registered overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 54 and the side supply passages 28 that was established at closure persists through the journey." findings.fix: Replace the sentence with: "The resilient feet 58 maintain a downward holding force during transport, so the registered overlap between the peripheral outlet openings 54 and the side supply passages 28 that was established at closure persists through the journey."

It has a near long side wall, a far long side wall, a left short end wall, a right short end wall and a bottom panel joining them." (merging with the following sentence and deleting the proportion clauses).

findings.title: FIG. 2 brief fixes a count and corner placement for the resilient feet

findings.detail: The brief specifies that the rib is formed integrally with the lid. The disclosure says only that the lid "carries" a depending indexing rib, which does not state how the rib is attached. Integral formation is a connection detail that conveys technical substance.

findings.title: The description contradicts itself and claim 1 on where the perforations deliver the descending air

findings.detail: One passage has the perforations delivering the descending stream into the product region along the tray length; another passage, both independent apparatus claims, the method claim, the abstract and the disclosure route the descending stream through the perforations and then through the lower return passage, from which it rises through the product region. findings.evidence: Candidate A: "Perforations 30 through the product tray 20 open from the side supply passages 28 into the product region and into the lower return passage 24." and "air delivered by the side supply passages 28 enters the product region along that length rather than at a single point." Source (disclosure.md line 7): "enters the side supply passages, passes through perforations in the product tray, and returns through the lower return passage."
findings.fix: Delete the two Candidate A statements (they are also unsupported, per the perforation finding above) and replace the first with: "Perforations 30 through the product tray 20 open from the side supply passages 28 into the lower return passage 24." findings.title: Peripheral outlet openings 54 and discharge openings 76 are recited at the identical location with nothing distinguishing them

findings.detail: Two different numbered elements are both defined as being "at lower ends of the guide ducts". findings.title: Sectional views carry no section line and no source view, and the fragmentary views are not tied to FIG. 1
findings.where: draft/07-drawings.md, FIGS. 1, 3, 4 and 5; figures/fig-01.md, fig-03.md, fig-04.md, fig-05.md
